title: Rust-JS FearCore Cross-Tree Parity Vectors
revision_note: 1.1.0 (2026-10-12): the Rust column is now MEASURED. Every vector carries a rust_scenario that tools/codegen/generate_rust_fear_oracle.mjs executes against the real fear.rs (results: evidence/rust_fear_oracle_results.json). VEC-12 expected_rust_band corrected Panicked -> Calm (1.0.0 asserted the JS behaviour for Rust). Added VEC-12b/12c and exit-side/skip-side vectors 17-19. Divergences are now declared per vector and the probe fails if a declared divergence does not occur or an undeclared one does.

nomenclature_mapping.Routed: ROUTED (Rust Core / JS Extended via IntentResolver)

declared_divergences.B1: Locked panic: Rust holds the lock only while score >= exit.afraid (0.8); JS holds it at any score.
declared_divergences.B3: Exit side, Panicked: Rust cascades Panicked -> Calm/Alert/Afraid in one evaluation by score; JS steps PANIC -> ANXIOUS only.
declared_divergences.B4: Exit side, Afraid: Rust Afraid below exit.alert goes straight to Calm; JS ANXIOUS goes to ALERT first.
declared_divergences.B5: Entry side, Alert: Rust Alert can jump to Panicked/Routed in one evaluation; JS ALERT goes to ANXIOUS first.
declared_divergences.B6: Entry side, Calm: Rust Calm can jump to Routed/Panicked in one evaluation; JS CALM goes to ALERT only (one band per update).
declared_divergences.B11: Routed (enter 4.6 / exit 3.0) is a Rust core band with no JS core band; JS handles >= 4.6 through IntentResolver and panic bias.

threshold_parity_matrix.parity_match: ADVISORY_PARITY (Rust 5th core band; JS handles 4.6+ via IntentResolver FLEE_FROM/PANIC and panic bias)

consecutive_lock_hold.description: After entering panic, how many further consecutive evaluations at score 1.0 (>= 0.8) stay in panic. Equal on both sides when evaluations are consecutive.

sparse_host_tick_release.description: B7. Rust's lock clock is the host eval_tick; JS counts update() calls. Entered at host tick 10, next evaluation at host tick 25 with score 1.0: Rust has released, JS (one update later) is still locked.

lock_without_eval_tick.description: B7. Rust arms no lock when eval_tick is None. JS has no tick parameter and always arms one.

lock_rearm.description: B8. Rust Panicked -> Routed keeps the existing lock (no re-arm). JS re-arms a fresh lock on every re-entry to PANIC from an extended band. These are different transitions (JS has no Routed), so this records behaviour, not a like-for-like comparison.

score_clamp.description: B9. Rust clamps the score to [0, 5]; JS floors at 0 only and records the raw value. Band outcomes are unaffected.

berserk_vs_aggressive.description: B10. Rust BerserkOverride is absorbing; JS AGGRESSIVE exits when anger falls below its exit threshold.

boundary_test_vectors.note: CORRECTED 2026-10-12. 1.0.0 recorded expected_rust_band=Panicked with the note 'score 0.0 cannot break panic'; that describes JS. Real Rust only holds a locked Panicked band while score >= exit.afraid (0.8), so at 0.0 it falls through to Calm. JS holds the lock at any score.
Just below Rust's lock-hold score (0.8): Rust leaves Panicked (to Alert, because 0.79 >= exit.alert 0.55); JS still holds.
At exactly Rust's lock-hold score (0.8) both engines hold: the one lock-active score region where they agree besides >= 1.2.
From ANXIOUS, extreme input enters the top core band in both engines: Rust's top band is Routed, JS's is PANIC (JS has no Routed core band).

boundary_test_vectors.architectural_distinction: Rust resolve_band evaluates multi-tier thresholds in a single tick (Calm -> Routed/Panicked), whereas JS FearCore enforces a 1-band-per-tick hysteresis ladder (Calm -> Alert -> Anxious -> Panic) unless an extended band override is triggered.

boundary_test_vectors.note: Exit side. Rust resolves the whole cascade by score in one evaluation; JS steps down one band per update.
Exit side. Rust Afraid below exit.alert (0.55) goes straight to Calm; JS ANXIOUS goes to ALERT first.
Entry side. Rust Alert jumps to Panicked in one evaluation; JS ALERT goes to ANXIOUS first.
